title: Texas judgment liens: when an abstract of judgment becomes a lien
rule: Once recorded and indexed, an abstract of a judgment that is not dormant is a lien on the debtor's real property in that county, including property acquired later, except property exempt from forced sale such as a homestead. The lien generally lasts 10 years from recording and indexing and ends sooner if the judgment goes dormant; state judgments last longer. During an appeal, a court finding can keep an abstract from becoming a lien where the debtor has posted, or is excused from posting, security.
changeWatch: Amendments to Property Code chapter 52 or to the judgment dormancy rule in Civil Practice and Remedies Code 34.001.

sources.title: Texas Property Code, Chapter 52 (Judgment liens)
